exposure: expectantly managed and delivered at 39 weeks of gestation or greater
expectantly managed infants delivered at 39-40 weeks of gestation
elective induction at 37-38 weeks of gestation
elective cesarean at 37-38 weeks of gestation
outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: 675,302 singleton infants born alive at 37-44 weeks of gestation in Florida from 2005 to 2009
finding: Elective induction at 37-38 weeks was not associated with increased odds of most adverse neonatal outcomes compared to expectant management and delivery at 39-40 weeks, while elective cesarean at 37-38 weeks was associated with significantly increased odds of adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Infants delivered by elective cesarean at 37-38 weeks had a 13-66% increased odds of adverse outcomes compared to those delivered at 39-40 weeks after expectant management.
